paper.paper_scope: Three hot-rolled austenitic low-density steels (Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.9C, Fe-28Mn-9Al-5Ni-0.9C and Fe-15Mn-9Al-5Ni-0.9C) were investigated to deconvolute the role of secondary phases, in particular the B2 ordered Fe(Ni)Al phase, on microstructure, strength, ductility and strain hardening behaviour after hot rolling.
paper.title: Microstructure and deformation behaviour of austenitic low-density steels: The defining role of B2 intermetallic phase

processes.description: Homogenised ingot hot rolled at 1323 K to a total thickness reduction of ~85% (~15% reduction per pass); final hot-rolled plate studied mechanically and microstructurally.

source.reason: The defect-free portions of the 30 kg ingots were homogenised at 1423 K for two hours, and micrographs are presented for the as-cast plus homogenised condition of all three alloys.
The Ni-free grade 28Mn0Ni (Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.9C) was examined in the hot-rolled condition for microstructure and tensile behaviour.
The Ni-containing high-Mn grade 28Mn5Ni (Fe-28Mn-9Al-5Ni-0.9C) was studied in the hot-rolled condition for microstructure and mechanical behaviour.

The low-Mn Ni-containing grade 15Mn5Ni (Fe-15Mn-9Al-5Ni-0.9C) was studied in the hot-rolled condition; it contains coarse B2 stringers and served as the primary B2-containing alloy for deformation studies.
Optical micrographs of 28Mn0Ni are presented for the as-cast plus homogenised condition (homogenised at 1423 K for 2 h).
Optical micrographs of 28Mn5Ni are presented for the as-cast plus homogenised condition.
Optical micrographs of 15Mn5Ni are presented for the as-cast plus homogenised condition; its B2 fraction in the as-cast state (~15%) is compared with the hot-rolled state.

unmapped_findings: Tensile tests on the hot-rolled 15Mn5Ni alloy were performed along both the rolling direction (RD) and the transverse direction (TD) to assess in-plane tensile anisotropy; the flow curves in RD and TD were almost identical, indicating minimal tensile anisotropy after hot rolling.

B2 phase volume fractions in the hot-rolled alloys were ~0.5%, ~4% and ~12% for 28Mn0Ni, 28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni respectively; for 15Mn5Ni it dropped from ~15% in the as-cast condition to ~12% after hot rolling at 1323 K.

Localised nanoindentation of the gamma-matrix and B2 stringer grains gave similar hardness (~6.7-6.8 GPa) and reduced moduli (~169-172 GPa), with B2 grains showing distinct pop-in events (~50-200 microN first pop-in loads) absent in the gamma-grains.

Chemical analysis of phases: B2 stringers in 15Mn5Ni were Fe-11.3Mn-12.2Al-7.4Ni (SEM-EDS) and Fe-10.1Mn-9.7Al-8.3Ni (TEM-EDS), while B2 in 28Mn5Ni was Fe-16.3Mn-13.6Al-21.5Ni (wt.%); the DO3 phase coexists with B2 with an orientation relationship [011]B2 || [011]DO3.
